title: Peter Chrysologus (30 July)
hook: golden-worded bishop of Ravenna known for short sermons
tomorrow: Our Lady of the Snows (5 August)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Martha, Mary and Lazarus, the household at Bethany. Your line was the house at bethany.

A sermon that ends while people are still paying attention. Not the homily that circles the runway before it lands. Today's saint aimed for the first kind. He was a bishop in the Italian city of Ravenna, he preached often, and tradition remembers him for keeping it short, so his people wouldn't tire and lose the thread. Along the way he was given a second name, a nickname that stuck so well it replaced his own. Today, the bishop with the golden word.
screen: `A SERMON THAT ENDS IN TIME.` → `A BISHOP OF RAVENNA.` → `A NICKNAME THAT STUCK.`

segments.voice: His name was Peter. Chrysologus came later. It's Greek, and tradition says it means golden-worded, a title given for the way he spoke. Sermons under his name have come down to us, and they are brief: one idea, opened up, and done. A line from the wisdom books fits him. In the Douay-Rheims, Ecclesiastes says: "therefore let thy words be few." The verse gives its reason just before: God is in heaven, and you are on earth. Few words aren't a lack of things to say. They're a kind of respect, for God and for the person listening. One of the sermons attributed to him is still read in the Church's prayer during Lent. It ties three practices together: prayer, fasting and mercy. In his picture they belong to each other and shouldn't be pulled apart. Prayer knocks, fasting obtains, mercy receives. If you pray but never show mercy, he says in effect, you've cut the thread. He fits a lot into a small space. That's the gift of a short word: it has to carry weight, so you choose it carefully. The Church honors him as a teacher of the faith, and a whole teaching is folded into his nickname. Say what is true, say it well, and stop. Gold is heavy. A little goes a long way.
screen: `PETER, THEN CHRYSOLOGUS.` · `ONE IDEA, AND DONE.` · `PRAYER, FASTING, MERCY TOGETHER.` · `SAY IT WELL, THEN STOP.` · then, large: `THEREFORE LET THY WORDS BE FEW.`

segments.voice: Think of someone you need to say something to: thank you, or sorry, or I'm proud of you, or I'm worried. Cut it down to one sentence, as few words as it can hold, and turn it over until it's simple and true. If you pray, offer God a short word too; if you don't, rest in the quiet after the sentence.
Peter Chrysologus. A bishop of Ravenna whose short sermons earned him a Greek nickname that tradition says means golden-worded.
Your line: short and golden. A few true words can be enough. That's day one thousand thirteen.

'The Church honors him as a teacher of the faith' stands in for Doctor of the Church; confirm whether to name the title.
